Help

How do I translate a transcript?

With Verbi Pro, open a recording and tap a language in the Translation card: English, Türkçe, Deutsch, Français, Español, Português (Brasil), Italiano, Русский, العربية, 日本語, 한국어, Bahasa Indonesia, Nederlands, Polski or 简体中文. The translation appears under the original transcript, which stays as it is; other target languages aren’t available.

Free to download, with 60 minutes of transcription every month.

Last updated: October 26, 2026

How do I translate a recording?

  1. Open the recording.
  2. Find the Translation card on the transcript. On the free plan, it shows “Upgrade to Pro for translation”.
  3. Tap a language: English, Türkçe, Deutsch, Français, Español, Português (Brasil), Italiano, Русский, العربية, 日本語, 한국어, Bahasa Indonesia, Nederlands, Polski or 简体中文.
  4. The translation appears under the original. To remove it, tap the selected language again, or the ✕.

Can Verbi translate while it transcribes?

Yes, with Pro. After you stop a recording, the completion screen shows Transcript Language, set to the app’s language. If the recording is in another language, Verbi adds a translation into the chosen language automatically after transcription. Free users don’t see this setting.

Limits

  • Translation is part of Verbi Pro on iPhone and Android.
  • Target languages: the 15 app languages, English, Turkish, German, French, Spanish, Portuguese (Brazil), Italian, Russian, Arabic, Japanese, Korean, Indonesian, Dutch, Polish and Simplified Chinese. Portuguese and Italian came with version 1.4.0 on iPhone and 1.2.0 on Android; the other eight came with 1.5.0 on iPhone and 1.3.0 on Android.
  • The recording itself can be in any of the 39 transcription languages.
  • For very long recordings, up to 200,000 characters of the transcript are translated.
  • To translate, the transcript text is sent to OpenAI.

Frequently asked questions

Can I translate into Italian, Portuguese or Arabic?

Yes, into all three: Italian and Portuguese (Brazil) from version 1.4.0 on iPhone and 1.2.0 on Android, and Arabic from version 1.5.0 on iPhone and 1.3.0 on Android. Transcription languages that aren’t among the 15 app languages, such as Ukrainian, aren’t translation targets, but Verbi still transcribes recordings in them.

Does the translation replace the original transcript?

No. It appears under the original, which stays as it is.

Is translation free?

No. It’s part of Verbi Pro.
